messages:
Mia (AE): Heads-up — Connective Health POC is scheduled for next Tue. They pushed back on a few items in the security questionnaire: SCIM provisioning at scale, SAML encrypted assertions, multi-domain ownership proof, and RBAC role mapping. Also asking about Dedicated pricing vs hosted for SSO traffic spikes. Need quick reps from SE/Eng/Security to confirm any hard blockers.
Diego (SE): I can take the SCIM/RBAC side. Quick Q: will they be provisioning 100k+ users in the POC or just a delta sync?
Mia (AE): POC will import ~25k users initial, then expect daily SCIM deltas ~2k. They said full rollouts could be larger, but for evaluation we need to show delta performance + bulk import path.
Diego (SE): OK. For 25k initial import we usually recommend the bulk CSV import (offline) + SCIM delta for ongoing. Hosted SCIM has a rate-limit we can relax for POCs with an SE-run throttle policy. @Sam can confirm env/ops constraints.
Sam (Eng): We can enable a temporary higher SCIM window for the POC (non-prod tenant) — typical approach: bump to 200 req/min for 48h and enable chunked PATCH support. No code changes. For Dedicated we'd provision a higher baseline if committed.
Ben (Security): On SAML: they ask for encrypted assertions (AES-256). We support assertion encryption with customer public certs. Need to confirm whether they want encrypted NameID as well. Also noted strict audience and recipient checking in their questionnaire.
Mia (AE): They did ask to encrypt whole assertion + NameID. Is that supported without extra infra?
Sam (Eng): Yup — in hosted we accept their SP metadata with encryption cert. We will include recipient and audience restrictions per metadata. Edge case: if they use multiple SP endpoints across domains we need separate metadata entries or an explicit multi-entity config.
Rachel (PM): For domain ownership: they require domain TXT proof for each consumer tenant domain and DNS automation for provisioning. We support domain verification via DNS TXT and via email for single domains. Automating multi-domain proofing at scale is product work — we can do manual verification for the POC (security ok) and propose automated DNS flow in the roadmap.
Diego (SE): For RBAC — they want role-to-permission mapping sync from their identity provider. SCIM supports group->role mapping. We can supply mapping rules on the SE side. Example mapping snippet we've used:
```
SCIM group displayName: "connective-admins" -> Redwood role: "org.admin"
SCIM group metadata custom:role_scope -> map to internal route-level perms
```
Mia (AE): Nice. They also worry about session timeouts and SSO session revocation on SCIM deprovision.
Ben (Security): Session revocation on deprovision is supported via our session invalidation webhook. We will need a bounded SLA for propagation in hosted (usually < 30s) and configurable for Dedicated. Note: if they have a long session TTL set on client side it can persist until token expiry. Recommend short TTL + immediate revoke on SCIM DELETE.
Anna (Legal): Two commercial asks: 1) If they choose Dedicated, do we need a data processing addendum (DPA) + SOC2 attestation? 2) They want explicit contractual language around domain proofing responsibility. I'll draft standard clauses but want technical notes to align.
Rachel (PM): For Dedicated: we expect a minimum commit (monthly) to justify reserved capacity. Pricing delta depends on GPU sizing and throughput targets. I can get a rough pricing band once Eng gives expected QPS for authentication+SCIM ops during peak.
Diego (SE): For the POC traffic likely: auth SAML handshake ~10 QPS peak, SCIM delta bursts up to 50 QPS for short windows during imports. KV cache and batching make generation cost small. That should map to a hosted tier with a short burst allowance; Dedicated only if sustained throughput > 200 QPS or strict isolation requested.
Mia (AE): Connective specifically asked: can we do POC in a VPC (private) since they're in healthcare?
Sam (Eng): Private (VPC) POCs are doable but take ~2 weeks to provision (networking + baseline infra). Hosted with private endpoints + strict data-at-rest controls is faster (48–72h) and usually acceptable for short POCs.
Ben (Security): For healthcare: KMS integration is required for encryption-at-rest keys. Hosted supports customer-managed keys via our KMS integration; Dedicated/private supports HSM if requested. We'll need their KMS ARN and IAM cross-account role for setup.
Mia (AE): Great — can we summarize blockers to present to customer?
Diego (SE): Blockers: none technical for POC if we accept manual domain verification and temporary SCIM rate bump. Need SE/Eng to schedule the rate bump window.
Sam (Eng): Ops tasks: provision temp SCIM throttle, add multi-metadata SAML entries, enable session-revoke webhook. ETA: 24–48h after we get SP metadata, SCIM base URL, and example CSV for import.
Ben (Security): Security checklist items to close: certs for assertion encryption, KMS ARN for key handling, confirmation of session TTL policy, and acceptance of manual domain TXT for POC.
Anna (Legal): I'll queue DPA + updated domain responsibility language. Need to know if customer requires SOC2 in contract (they indicated yes).
Mia (AE): Perfect. I'll collect the SP metadata and sample CSV today and send to @Diego and @Sam. Can we get a short doc/snippet I can share with them for the security questionnaire?
Diego (SE): I'll drop a one-pager with recommended answers + required artifacts (SP metadata, KMS ARN, admin contact) by EOD.
Sam (Eng): I'll prepare the ops runbook for the rate bump and session webhook and post it here when ready.
deploy-bot: Deployment scheduled: "poc-scim-throttle-config" will be applied to staging in 2h — notify if you need rollback. :rocket:
Mia (AE): Thanks all — I'll sync with the customer and escalate any contract asks. :thumbsup:
